lines.name: Main line (4.Nc3 dxc4)
lines.intro: In the Slav you defend d5 with ...c6, so your light-squared bishop can come out to f5 before ...e6. In the main line you take on c4, then develop and castle.

notes.0: White opens with the queen's pawn.
notes.1: Claim your share of the center.
notes.2: The Queen's Gambit: White offers a pawn.
notes.3: The Slav: defend d5 with the c-pawn and keep the c8 bishop free.
notes.7: Take the pawn. White will spend time winning it back.
notes.8: White stops ...b5, so you can't keep the pawn.
notes.9: Get the bishop out before ...e6. This is the point of the Slav.
notes.10: White prepares to win back c4.
notes.11: Now ...e6 doesn't lock in your bishop.
notes.13: Pin the knight so White can't easily push e4.
notes.15: Castle too. You have a solid, comfortable position.

lines.name: Exchange (3.cxd5)
lines.intro: White trades on d5 for a symmetrical structure. Develop actively, copy White's setup where it makes sense, and watch the c-file.

notes.0: White opens with the queen's pawn.
notes.1: Claim your share of the center.
notes.2: The Queen's Gambit: White offers a pawn.
notes.3: The Slav: defend d5 with the c-pawn and keep the c8 bishop free.
notes.5: Take back. The position is symmetrical.
notes.8: White develops the bishop outside the pawn chain.
notes.11: Copy White: get your bishop out before ...e6.

lines.name: vs. 4.e3
lines.intro: Against the quiet 4.e3, develop the bishop to f5 anyway. If White chases it with Nh4, drop back to g6, and take back with the h-pawn if it's traded.

notes.0: White opens with the queen's pawn.
notes.1: Claim your share of the center.
notes.2: The Queen's Gambit: White offers a pawn.
notes.3: The Slav: defend d5 with the c-pawn and keep the c8 bishop free.
notes.6: White supports d4 and opens the f1 bishop, but shuts in the c1 bishop.
notes.7: Get the bishop out before ...e6. This is the main idea of the Slav.
notes.9: Now ...e6 is safe: your bishop is already outside the pawn chain.
notes.10: White chases the bishop to win the bishop pair.
notes.11: Keep the bishop on its diagonal.
notes.13: Take back with the h-pawn. Your rook gets a half-open h-file.
